title: China's 2015 Market Crash: How a Bubble Became a Feedback Loop
objective: Explain the mechanics of China's 2015 equity crash as a compact, factual vertical story: a policy-fuelled rally, leveraged buying, forced selling, and a rescue that could slow but not reverse a confidence shock.
audience: Curious mobile viewers who understand markets broadly but want a visual model of how a crash feeds on itself.

message.core_message: Leverage turns a falling market into a feedback loop: losses trigger forced selling, forced selling pushes prices lower, and confidence becomes the scarce asset.
key_points: The Shanghai Composite more than doubled between mid-2014 and its June 2015 peak.
The index then lost roughly one-third in less than a month.
Margin finance amplified the move because collateral shrank as prices fell.
State intervention can add liquidity, but it cannot instantly restore risk appetite.

constraints: Use a warm light canvas and readable mobile typography
Every spoken section must develop visually at least every 2-3 seconds
Treat historical figures as approximate where sources differ

references.description: Existing local China Market Crash recreations and rendered previews; inspected for pacing, vertical hierarchy, and data-storytelling techniques only. No copy, branding, footage, or shot sequence is reused.

audio.notes: Documentary narration, quiet modular pulse bed, and only tactile data/alert accents.

research.reason: The project makes historical and market-mechanics claims that require a source-backed research dossier.

creative_directions.name: Editorial Cascade
creative_directions.concept: An ivory financial notebook becomes a living market machine: an optimistic curve climbs, collateral drains, orders funnel through a narrow book, and a rescue stamp meets a confidence gap.

visual_identity.palette: Ivory, charcoal, vermilion, ultramarine, marigold and emerald
visual_identity.typography: Bold sans display with compact monospace data
visual_identity.texture: Paper grain, chart ink and translucent glass cards

motion_language.personality: Measured at first, then progressively compressed and urgent

composition.approach: One dominant vertical visual per chapter, with a persistent chapter rail and 65%+ stage occupancy
composition.portrait: Headline above a 320-850px hero stage; takeaway card above the bottom safe zone

creative_directions.pacing: Four chapters with three to five micro-beats each.
creative_directions.why_it_fits: It carries factual density without becoming a terminal dashboard.

creative_directions.name: Newsroom Tape
creative_directions.concept: A clipped press-desk aesthetic with ticker strips, timestamp cards and hard data labels.

visual_identity.palette: Newsprint cream, black, signal red and cobalt

creative_directions.why_it_fits: High energy, but risks crowding a small screen.

creative_directions.name: Minimal Proof
creative_directions.concept: A calm visual proof of the leverage equation, with only a curve, balance sheet and feedback-loop arrows.

visual_identity.palette: White, ink, amber and one red warning

creative_directions.why_it_fits: Clear, but underplays the human panic dimension.

selection_rationale: The selected direction makes the feedback loop legible on a phone while keeping a serious, source-led tone.
success_criteria: No visual hold longer than two seconds during narration
All type is legible at 720px portrait
Final video has 720x1280 H.264 video and AAC audio
